newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT- Staples, Office Depot.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT- Staples, Office Depot.

text.p: Staples Inc and Office Depot Inc said Monday they will vigorously pursue their proposed $4 billion merger and seek an expedited court hearing following the Federal Trade Commission's rejection of the transaction last week.
A full text of the release follows.

Staples, Inc. (NASDAQ:SPLS) and Office Depot, Inc. (NYSE: ODP) today announced that both companies have agreed to vigorously contest the recent Federal Trade Commission (FTC) ruling against a proposed settlement as contemplated under the merger agreement and to aggressively pursue completion of the merger. The parties intend to seek an expedited hearing to resolve the issue before a federal judge prior to the May 31, 1997 expiration of the parties merger agreement.

Thomas G. Stemberg, chairman and chief executive officer, Staples, Inc., said, "We believe an unbiased court of law will understand the merits of our case. The FTC clearly lacks an understanding of the office products industry. Staples and Office Depot as a combined company will have less than a 6% share of a highly competitive and largely fragmented $185 billion office products industry. Virtually all 8,000 products we sell are readily available at numerous strong competitors including other office supply stores, contract stationers, mail order catalog dealers, discount stores, drug stores and wholesale clubs."

He continued, "Once again the FTC has placed themselves between our customers and lower prices. Each month that passes costs our customers over $40 million in savings. Staples and Office Depot are committed to our mission of bringing even lower prices to our customers. In fact, just last month Staples passed on cost savings in the form of lower prices on hundreds of office supplies in every market in which we have stores. As a combined company, Staples/Office Depot will be better positioned to save customers even more money."

David I. Fuente, chairman and chief executive officer of Office Depot, said, "The merger between Office Depot and Staples is a win-win situation for everyone involved. Our customers will save even more. We anticipate a net increase in employment at the combined company. The transaction is anticipated to be accretive to shareholders of both companies. Additionally, the merger will better enable the companies to expand internationally and compete successfully in a global economy. For the FTC to continue to fight this merger is inappropriate in every respect."

Staples, Inc. currently operates 585 office product superstores in over 150 markets throughout North America, including 496 stores in the US and 87 in Canada. The company operates a mail order business, "Staples Direct," and has contract stationer operations named "Staples Business Advantage" and "Staples National Advantage," which serve the needs of large regional and national corporations, respectively. Staples operates 50 stores in England and Germany.

Office Depot currently operates 572 stores in over 200 markets throughout North America, including 536 stores in the US and 36 stores in Canada, in addition to a national business-to-business delivery network. Office Depot also has joint ventures or licensed operations in Mexico, Israel, Poland, Thailand, France, Colombia and Japan.
